value.rationale: A symmetric centrally restarted absorbing interval is a natural physical transport geometry. The threshold shows material heterogeneity alone reverses the effectiveness of weak restart even when geometry is symmetric; the exact critical quadratic coefficient distinguishes marginal slowdown from neutrality. The unequal-layer formula unifies geometry and material response, and the local-onset law quantifies near-threshold engineering tradeoffs. Narrowly model-specific and no global optimum is claimed.
